blocking_findings.exact_text: The bridge was dropping, and the line, still clipped to his harness and pulled taut by the falling span, dragged him backward.
blocking_findings.reason: The line was tied to a trunk and held by Nisa, not attached to the bridge, so the falling span could not pull it taut. Cutting it is then unnecessary.

blocking_findings.exact_text: Cutting the line had saved him.
blocking_findings.reason: Cutting is framed as the rescue, but the line is not shown connected to the falling bridge, so the causal claim is unsupported.

blocking_findings.exact_text: he cut the line from his harness
blocking_findings.reason: The line was tied to a trunk and Nisa caught its free end; the harness clip is not established. Cutting the line also strands it with the bridge.

blocking_findings.exact_text: found the great root span still hooked to its far anchor, its near anchor torn loose
blocking_findings.reason: They approach from the camp and Arda crossed the bridge heading inland, so near and far anchors and sides are confused with the later rescue.

editorial_advisories.exact_text: Their gliders still lay on the shore, waiting.
editorial_advisories.reason: Nisa's glider landing is never shown, and the gliders were never staked down against the wind and mist.

editorial_advisories.exact_text: "I'll be back soon; if the light starts to dim, that's our signal to turn back.
editorial_advisories.reason: Nisa says she will return soon, and her promise is oddly repeated; it conflicts with S082's 'we promised... careful' tone. Minor timing and wording mismatch.
Narration in close third person hedges awkwardly with 'presumably' and 'certainly'.

editorial_advisories.exact_text: It was not like any pattern he'd ever seen.
editorial_advisories.reason: Redundant with the preceding sentence 'not any pattern currently taught'; also 'almost recognized' contradicts it.

editorial_advisories.exact_text: Arda brought the glider in at an angle, half-flying and half-falling
editorial_advisories.reason: Minor: the beats call for the rope to be the cut climax, but its tie-off logic deviates from the spine's rescue-line role.

editorial_advisories.exact_text: but not any pattern currently taught
editorial_advisories.reason: “Not any pattern” is an unnatural determiner construction here; idiomatic English uses “not one currently taught.”

editorial_advisories.exact_text: not like any pattern he'd ever seen
editorial_advisories.reason: A hitch more naturally “matches” a pattern; “was not like any pattern” sounds imprecise and slightly non-native.
The repeated “with” and intervening comma awkwardly separate two parallel things filling the pages.

editorial_advisories.exact_text: you got off it in time
editorial_advisories.reason: “Got off” gives an unclear physical relationship to the line; “cut yourself free” directly and naturally describes the action.

entry_boundary.text: "Hurry, the light's dimming and the wind is picking up," he said.

exit_boundary.text: He pulled himself up onto solid root, breathing like a bellows, and looked back at the gap where the bridge had been.

canon_invariants: The light expedition line briefly steadies the glider at the shore landing, then is unfastened, coiled and carried inland. It serves as the rescue line at the root bridge, and cutting it there at the climax is a sacrifice.

The glider catches a root and tilts, but holds. Arda briefly lashes the route line to a stout trunk to steady the glider while they get their footing. Before they go inland he unfastens it, coils it and slings it over his shoulder to carry with him.

Arda and Nisa race back through the mist-filled forest. The root bridge has torn loose in the wind, so Arda uncoils the route line he has carried from the shore, swings Nisa across with it, and then cuts the line loose to free himself.
The line is lost and the bridge falls into the cloud sea.
Arda finds that his own trust in Nisa's timing is what saves him.
They reach the shore with the glider tag and journal, but the route line is gone and with it any marked return point.
Their last launch must be flown without the line, with the corridor nearly shut.
Cutting the carried route line to save himself and Nisa on the collapsing root bridge, then flying the last open stretch of the corridor with no line left as the cloud wall seals behind them.
Arda and Nisa launch from the sloping beach, catching the last updraft and flying toward the narrow corridor with the island sliding away behind them.
The corridor closes behind them as they reach known sky, and the island dissolves into the cloud wall.
They land safely at Stormbreak Watch, shaken and carrying the one proof that matters.

Arda and Nisa bring home the journal and the glider-tag, concrete proof that an earlier expedition reached the island and intended to return. They are not the first, and their friendship is stronger for the honest argument and the shared escape. The island's origin and destination remain unknown.

scene_repair_handoff.source_scene:
They hurried back toward the bridge Arda had crossed.

The bridge could not hold much longer. They came down through the mist-filled trees at a dead run and found the great root span still hooked to its anchor on the far side, its near anchor torn loose, thrashing in the wind above a drop into the cloud sea. Mist rolled around their knees, cold and fast.

"Line," Nisa said. No argument this time. Just the word.

Arda uncoiled the route line he'd carried from the shore. He tied one end to the last living trunk on his side, clipped the other end to his harness, swung the free end across the gap, and Nisa caught it and hauled herself across hand over hand while the wind tried to peel her off. She made it. She turned and held the line steady for him.

He got three-quarters of the way across before the far anchor of the bridge groaned.

He felt it—the shift, the give, the whole bridge lurching toward the drop with him still on it. The bridge was dropping, and the line, still clipped to his harness and caught on the falling span, dragged him backward. There was only one thing left to do, and he hated every second of it: he cut the line from his harness and let it fall away with the bridge.

The tension released at once. The bridge fell away beneath him into the cloud sea, and Arda lunged for the ledge where Nisa knelt. She leaned out and hauled; his hand found her wrist, and her grip found him. Cutting the line had freed him from the falling bridge. Her strong grip had done the rest.
